disclaimer: Microalgae gene data is primarily from the model green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (JGI genome v5.6) and Chlorella vulgaris (NCBI genome) — both of which have well-annotated reference genomes. Where species differ significantly, the source species is noted. Many bioenergy-relevant genes are well-characterized in these systems.

evidenceLevelKey.Peer-Reviewed Literature: Gene directly characterized in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, Chlorella vulgaris, or a closely related microalga in a published peer-reviewed study.
evidenceLevelKey.Curated Database Reference: Gene annotated in JGI Phytozome, NCBI, or a curated algal genomics database.
evidenceLevelKey.Homology-Based Projection: Gene inferred from a characterized ortholog in another photosynthetic organism.
evidenceLevelKey.Environment-Relevance Estimate: Pathway relevance inferred from algal physiology and biomass/biofuel literature.

genes.name: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase (rate-limiting step in fatty acid biosynthesis)
genes.functionSummary: Carboxylates acetyl-CoA to malonyl-CoA — the committed first step of de novo fatty acid biosynthesis in the chloroplast. ACCase is the primary rate-limiting enzyme for lipid accumulation in microalgae. Overexpression of ACCase increases fatty acid content; nitrogen starvation redirects carbon flux through this enzyme to triglyceride (TAG) accumulation for biodiesel production.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii CrACC1 (Cre06.g307950); Dunahay TG et al. 1996 Appl Biochem Biotechnol 57/58(1):223–231; Hu Q et al. 2008 Plant J 54(4):621–639
genes.limitationNote: ACCase overexpression alone does not always translate to proportional TAG increase — downstream steps also limit flux.

genes.name: Diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (TAG biosynthesis for biodiesel)
genes.functionSummary: Catalyzes the final acylation step in the Kennedy pathway — converting diacylglycerol (DAG) to triacylglycerol (TAG, the main component of biodiesel). DGAT1 expression is strongly induced by nitrogen starvation in microalgae, triggering the massive lipid accumulation characteristic of nutrient-stressed algae used for biodiesel production.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii CrDGAT1 (Cre12.g557750); Siaut M et al. 2011 BMC Genomics 12:366; Merchant SS et al. 2012 eLife 1:e00015
genes.limitationNote: DGAT1 and PDAT1 are the two primary TAG-synthesizing enzymes in Chlamydomonas; their relative contributions vary by strain and conditions.

genes.name: Phospholipid:diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1
genes.functionSummary: Transfers fatty acids from membrane phospholipids to DAG to form TAG. During nitrogen starvation, PDAT1 recycles membrane phospholipids (as chloroplasts are degraded) into storage TAG. This is a major route of lipid accumulation in Chlamydomonas — connecting membrane breakdown to oil storage.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii CrPDAT1 (Cre16.g695900); Yoon K et al. 2012 Plant Cell 24(9):3708–3724; Moellering ER, Benning C 2010 Science 329(5997):1318–1319
genes.limitationNote: PDAT1 and chloroplast lipid remodeling during N-starvation are well-studied in Chlamydomonas.

genes.name: Fatty acid thioesterase A (chain-length termination)
genes.functionSummary: Terminates fatty acid chain elongation by cleaving the acyl group from acyl-carrier protein (ACP). Thioesterase specificity determines the fatty acid chain length profile of the oil — critical for biodiesel quality. Engineering thioesterase variants can shift the fatty acid profile toward shorter chains (jet fuel range) or specific biodiesel-optimal lengths.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii fatty acid thioesterase; Jones A et al. 1995 Plant Cell 7(3):359–371; Radakovits R et al. 2010 Eukaryot Cell 9(4):486–501
genes.limitationNote: Thioesterase engineering for biofuel chain-length optimization is an active area of algal metabolic engineering.

genes.name: Rubisco large subunit (photosynthetic CO2 fixation)
genes.functionSummary: Primary CO2-fixing enzyme in microalgae. Microalgae have a CO2-concentrating mechanism (CCM) with pyrenoid-localized Rubisco, allowing efficient CO2 fixation even at low atmospheric CO2. Algae achieve 3–10× higher biomass productivity per unit area than terrestrial plants in optimized growth systems, largely due to efficient light capture and Rubisco utilization.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii rbcL (chloroplast gene); Merchant SS et al. 2007 Science 318(5848):245–250 (Chlamydomonas genome)
genes.limitationNote: rbcL is one of the best-studied genes in algae — the Chlamydomonas genome was a landmark in photosynthesis research.

genes.name: Light-harvesting complex II (antenna protein)
genes.functionSummary: Major light-harvesting antenna of photosystem II. LHCII trimers capture sunlight and funnel energy to the PSII reaction center. In dense algal cultures (photobioreactors), wild-type LHCII causes photoinhibition near the light surface while cells deeper in culture receive no light. Truncated LHCII strains improve culture-wide light penetration and biomass productivity.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii LHCBM genes; Mitra M, Melis A 2008 Planta 228(6):907–919; Polle JEW et al. 2002 Planta 214(4):496–503
genes.limitationNote: LHCII truncation for improved photobioreactor performance is one of the most studied algal bioenergy engineering targets.

genes.name: [FeFe]-hydrogenase 1 (biohydrogen production)
genes.functionSummary: Iron-iron hydrogenase that produces molecular hydrogen (H2) by coupling photosynthetically derived electrons to proton reduction. Under sulfur deprivation, Chlamydomonas switches from O2-evolving photosynthesis to anaerobic H2 production via HydA1. This is a potential pathway for solar-driven, carbon-free fuel production — a unique bioenergy pathway not available in terrestrial plants.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii HydA1 (Cre09.g396600); Melis A et al. 2000 Plant Physiol 122(1):127–136; Ghirardi ML et al. 2007 Trends Biotechnol 25(9):395–401
genes.limitationNote: H2 production rates are currently too low for commercial deployment — a major active research area in DOE and NREL programs.

genes.name: Nitrate reductase 1 (nitrogen assimilation / lipid accumulation control)
genes.functionSummary: Reduces nitrate to nitrite — first step in nitrogen assimilation. NIT1 activity governs how rapidly cells experience nitrogen starvation when nitrogen is withheld. Nitrogen starvation is the most powerful trigger for TAG (oil) accumulation in microalgae. Understanding NIT1 regulation helps control the timing of the growth-to-oil transition in algal biofuel production.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii NIT1 (Cre06.g274750); Fernandez E, Galvan A 2007 Trends Plant Sci 12(10):442–448; Miller R et al. 2010 Plant Cell 22(8):2783–2798
genes.limitationNote: NIT1 is a classical model gene in Chlamydomonas genetics — long used as a selectable marker and N-status indicator.

genes.name: Glycerol-3-phosphate acyltransferase (TAG backbone)
genes.functionSummary: Adds the first fatty acid to the glycerol-3-phosphate backbone — first committed step in glycerolipid biosynthesis. GPAT activity controls the initial carbon input to TAG synthesis. Both plastidic and ER-localized GPAT isoforms contribute to oil accumulation in microalgae.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii GPAT (Cre16.g691400 annotation); Zheng P et al. 2012 Genomics 100(6):401–406
genes.limitationNote: Multiple GPAT paralogs exist in microalgae; which are most relevant to TAG accumulation requires isoform-specific analysis.

genes.name: Manganese superoxide dismutase (ROS defense, photoinhibition protection)
genes.functionSummary: Mitochondrial Mn-SOD detoxifies superoxide generated by electron transport under high light and heat stress. In outdoor algal ponds (relevant to Texas bioenergy production), extreme summer radiation causes photoinhibition and ROS production. SOD activity is a key determinant of algal productivity under intense Texas sunlight.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii MSD1 (Cre17.g741950); Hanikenne M et al. 2001 FEBS Lett 498(2-3):188–192
genes.limitationNote: Chlamydomonas SOD enzymes are well-characterized; outdoor pond systems in Texas would expose algae to high UV and heat.

genes.name: Starch synthase (competing sink for photosynthate vs. lipids)
genes.functionSummary: Synthesizes starch granules as a primary carbon storage product. Under nitrogen replete conditions, Chlorella stores carbon primarily as starch; nitrogen starvation shifts partitioning toward TAG (oil). Downregulation of starch synthesis in microalgae often increases oil content — demonstrating direct competition between starch and lipid sinks for photosynthate.
genes.orthologSource: Chlorella vulgaris starch synthase; Brányiková I et al. 2011 Biotechnol Bioeng 108(4):766–776; Wang ZT et al. 2009 Eukaryot Cell 8(12):1856–1868
genes.limitationNote: Starch–lipid competition is well-established; blocking starch synthesis to increase oil content is a validated metabolic engineering strategy.

genes.name: Cytochrome b6f complex (electron transport chain)
genes.functionSummary: The cytochrome b6f complex transfers electrons from plastoquinol to plastocyanin, linking photosystem II to photosystem I. It also drives proton pumping across the thylakoid membrane, contributing to ATP synthesis. Cytb6f is often a limiting step in linear electron flow and thus a target for photosynthesis optimization.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii petA/B/D genes; Rochaix JD 1996 Plant Mol Biol 32(1-2):327–341
genes.limitationNote: Cyt b6f is a classical target in Chlamydomonas photosynthesis research — extensively characterized since the 1970s.

genes.name: Carbonic anhydrase 1 / CO2-concentrating mechanism activator (CIA5)
genes.functionSummary: CIA5 is the master transcriptional activator of the CO2-concentrating mechanism (CCM) in Chlamydomonas. CAH1 (periplasmic carbonic anhydrase) converts CO2 to bicarbonate for uptake. Together, the CCM pumps inorganic carbon into the pyrenoid where Rubisco is concentrated — allowing efficient CO2 fixation at low atmospheric CO2 levels.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii CIA5 (Cre02.g096100) / CAH1 (Cre01.g049000); Moroney JV, Ynalvez RA 2007 Eukaryot Cell 6(8):1251–1259
genes.limitationNote: The CCM is a defining feature of microalgal CO2 fixation efficiency — a major reason algae outperform terrestrial plants in productivity.

genes.name: Nitrogen response regulator NRR1 (N-starvation master regulator)
genes.pathwayName: Nitrogen Starvation Response — Oil Accumulation Trigger
genes.functionSummary: SQUAMOSA-promoter binding (SBP) domain transcription factor that activates the nitrogen starvation transcriptional response. NRR1 upregulates TAG biosynthesis genes, activates autophagy, and reprograms carbon flux from growth to oil storage under nitrogen starvation — the primary trigger for algal biodiesel production.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii NRR1 (Cre12.g519000); Boyle NR et al. 2012 Plant Cell 24(5):1860–1875
genes.limitationNote: NRR1 is a key master regulator of the N-starvation → oil accumulation switch in Chlamydomonas — well-characterized by the Benning lab (MSU).

genes.name: Fatty acid synthase / 3-ketoacyl-ACP synthase (chain elongation)
genes.functionSummary: KAS (3-ketoacyl-ACP synthase) enzymes condense malonyl-ACP with acyl-ACP to extend fatty acid chains by two carbons per cycle. KAS I (C4→C16), KAS II (C16→C18), and KAS III (C2→C4) together build the full-length fatty acid chain. The chain length profile of the final fatty acids determines biodiesel combustion properties.
genes.orthologSource: Chlorella vulgaris FAS complex; Morin N et al. 2019 Biotechnol Biofuels 12:106; Guschina IA, Harwood JL 2006 Prog Lipid Res 45(2):160–186
genes.limitationNote: Fatty acid composition in Chlorella is well-studied in the context of biodiesel production; KAS enzyme specificity determines chain length output.

genes.name: Photosystem II D1 protein (core reaction center, photoinhibition target)
genes.functionSummary: D1 is the primary reaction center protein of PSII and the most rapidly turned over protein in the chloroplast. Under high light stress — especially relevant for outdoor Texas algal ponds — D1 is photodamaged by reactive oxygen and must be rapidly replaced. The D1 repair cycle rate limits algal productivity under high irradiance.
genes.orthologSource: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii psbA (chloroplast gene); Takahashi S, Badger MR 2011 Trends Plant Sci 16(1):53–60; Aro EM et al. 1993 Biochim Biophys Acta 1143(2):113–134
genes.limitationNote: D1 photodamage and repair is one of the most-studied topics in photosynthesis — directly relevant to outdoor algal production in high-insolation Texas.
